>Once the Legacy of Pander is in play, are all Panders titled, or not?

No.

>What about vampires who have conditional votes if they burn blood,
>like that giovanni bloke,

Stefano. No, his card text doesn't have permanent votes, it has an
ability to gain some. It's only the vampires with permanent votes who
count.

> or anybody with Lyndhurst estate NY - are
>they titled, or not? [i'ld guess they aren't]

No.

How to work it out:

Does this vampire have a title on their card which they haven't lost?
Yes: They have a title.
Does this vampire have a permanent number of votes on their card which
they haven't lost?
Yes: They have a title.
Has this vampire been granted a title, by specific card text (e.g.
Ventrue Justicar)
Yes: They have a title.

You need vampire card text of title or permanent votes, or library text
granting a title, for it to count.

Messages.Author: Pat Ricochet
Messages.Body:
> No one still thinks it would be easier to just make all vampires with votes
> titled? Or just ignore independents and only make Named vampires 'titled.'
> Save lots of confusion and trouble. =/

Well, except for National Guard Support:
"Called by any titled vampire at +1 stealth..."
which was released in Final Nights, and obviously intended to be playable by
the titled independents.
However, consider:

Bob, generic Independent vampire
X-cap
ran DOM ski LLS
"Independent. Bob has N vote(s)."

EVERY titled independent vampire is titled in this manner. Not unlike
"Sabbat Cardinal." or
"Camarilla Primogen."
at the start of the card text.

Extremely simple litmus test to use. Saves lots of confusion and
trouble. If you prefer, think of "Bob has 1 vote." as a title worth 1
vote, and "Bob has 2 votes." as a title worth 2 votes.

After that, the only way to get a title is to play a card that gives you
a named title. That's it. Done.

If you WANT to make it hard and confusing to distinguish, you can ask
about this and that and the other, but if you're actually interested in
remembering, it only takes two simple rules, which are probably easier to
remember than whether or not you can play another bleed modifier after your
Conditioning has been DI'd. But, there are things you just have to remember
to play by the rules. Whether or not a vampire is titled is one of the
easier ones.
(I seem to recall all of this having been said before, but since people
are still having trouble with it...)

>> So...if there was some new equipment card making the bearer Independent, and

>> so...?
>
>It wouldn't affect Gratiano, since the Prisci referendum is not a vote
>per se. Therefore if he is and independant, he no longer is involved
>in the Prisci vote, so has not vote at all.

He has card text granting him a vote in the Prisci vote. He would no
longer be a Priscus, but he would still have the card text allowing him
a vote.

> I guess.
>
>Genevieve on the other hand has a fixed vote. As such, I guess she is
>titled in her own right.

No. As LSJ has already pointed out, this would involve her having two
titles at once, which cannot be true.

The intent, per [6.3.4] is to allow vampires who are independent
vampires by card text to have a title. [6.3.3] makes this slightly more
ambiguous, but the fact that, in these instances, they would have to
have two titles makes it clear that the card text is not a title.

>I heard somewhere that a vampire that Clan Impersonates to a different
>sect still keeps their votes and title, but cannot use them whilst
>"impersonating".

True. Section [10] of the rules book.

>This means that if they burn the imp, they get their
>old jobs back, votes and all.

If:

- no-one else has contested their title (which the CIed vampire would
immediately yield)
- the CIed vampire had not been granted another title appropriate to
their "pretend" clan/sect (thus yielding their dormant title)

they can get it back.

>If so, are they still titled whilst impersonating?

No. Being titled is a benefit. (For playing Free States Rant etc.)
Section [10] makes it clear he loses the benefit.

>For example, Sir Walter goes Deranged by his predator, making him

>him, no 5th trad, no 2 votes, etc.
>He then goes and bleeds his prey, who controls a Ravnos.
>During his prey's master phase, they want to play a "The Treatment" on
>Sir Walter. Is this allowed?

Per the restrictions thing with Seeds of Corruption, I'd say no.

Remember, in the right situation that could be a Good Thing. Maybe.
Noal, Legbiter and Xian will probably do odd things.

>Also, if Calebros The Martyr changes sects, thus losing the benefit of
>his title, but not actually losing the title, can older Cam vampires
>still steal it off him?

He's not considered the Prince of New York when non-Camarilla. (First
clause of card text.) The title still lingers ready for:

- a potential contesting (where he immediately yields it)
- going back to the relevant sect/clan

But the vampire isn't titled for effects. (Unless such an effect were
to say something like: "(D) Enter combat with a vampire who has a title
which has been rendered dormant by changing to an inappropriate
clan/sect" - but odd card texts like that always do things outside the
rules.)

Having the title is a benefit - sometimes a dubious one. You lose all
benefits, dubious or otherwise, when changing to an inappropriate
clan/sect.
